description: Risk assessment for a service to determine testing thoroughness (SE-02-A10)

risk_assessment_philosophy.purpose: Determine testing thoroughness based on risk, not uniform testing for all services
risk_assessment_philosophy.principle: Focus effort on high-risk services (payment, auth, data storage) while avoiding over-testing low-risk services (logging, metrics)
risk_assessment_philosophy.honesty: Be honest about risk - underestimating risk leads to insufficient testing and production failures
risk_assessment_philosophy.rationale_required: Every risk score must have documented rationale for future maintainers

risk_categories.description: Three independent risk categories, each scored 1-3 (low/medium/high)

deployment_risk.description: Complexity of deploying and configuring the service
deployment_risk.rationale: {Why this severity level? What factors led to this assessment?}
factors: Novel technology stack (new language/framework for team)
Extensive infrastructure dependencies (message queue, cache, search engine)
Complex configuration (50+ environment variables, intricate setup)
Database migrations with complex schema or data transformations

low.description: Simple stateless service, familiar tech stack
examples: REST API in Python/FastAPI (team knows Python)
CRUD service with PostgreSQL only
Static content API

medium.description: Moderate deployment complexity or semi-familiar tech
indicators: Somewhat familiar tech (team has some experience, not experts)
2-3 infrastructure dependencies (DB + Redis cache, or DB + MQ)
examples: Service with Redis cache + PostgreSQL
Service in newer framework (FastAPI for team used to Flask)
Service with background workers (Celery + Redis)

high.description: Complex deployment or unfamiliar tech stack
indicators: Novel tech stack (team has no prior experience)
4+ infrastructure dependencies (DB + MQ + cache + search + monitoring)
Database migrations with data transformations, complex constraints
examples: Service in language team doesn't know (Rust for Python team)
Distributed stateful service (Kafka, Elasticsearch cluster)
Service requiring complex infrastructure (K8s operators, service mesh)

integration_risk.description: Risk from dependencies on other services or external systems
integration_risk.rationale: {Why this severity level? What dependencies create risk?}
factors: Synchronous dependencies (service waits for response, blocks on failure)
External system dependencies (third-party APIs, payment gateways)
Tight coupling (assumes specific response format, no graceful degradation)
No circuit breakers or fallback mechanisms

indicators: No calls to other services (or only async event publishing)
examples: Logging service (writes to DB only)
Metrics collector (standalone aggregation)
Static content API (reads from DB only)
Notification service (calls user service async for user details)
Search service (calls 1-2 services for data enrichment, can return partial results)
Report generator (publishes events, doesn't wait for processing)

high.description: Synchronous dependencies on 3+ services or external systems
indicators: External API dependencies (payment gateway, shipping API, third-party auth)
Tight coupling (service fails if dependency unavailable)
Complex dependency chains (service A → B → C)
Real-time requirements (can't tolerate latency or failures)
examples: API gateway (calls 5+ backend services synchronously)
Payment service (calls external payment gateway + fraud detection + user service)
Checkout service (calls inventory + pricing + tax + shipping services)

operational_risk.description: Impact of service failure on system and business
operational_risk.rationale: {Why this severity level? What is the impact of failure?}
factors: On critical path (user-facing, revenue-generating, blocks core functionality)
Data integrity critical (financial transactions, health data, PII)
No redundancy or failover (single point of failure)

indicators: Not on critical path (background job, analytics, reporting)
Low traffic (< 100 req/sec or batch processing)
Has redundancy or can be temporarily unavailable
Failure doesn't block users or revenue
examples: Logging service (can buffer logs temporarily)
Analytics pipeline (batch jobs, can run delayed)
Email service (can retry sends, not blocking)
Metrics aggregation (can tolerate gaps)

medium.description: Important feature, has degraded mode or redundancy
indicators: Important data but not financial/health (user preferences, search history)
Has degraded mode or fallback (can return cached data, default values)
Failure affects some users but not all
examples: Search service (can return cached results or no results)
Recommendation service (can show default recommendations)
Notification service (can queue for later, not blocking)
User profile service (can show partial profile)

high.description: Critical path, high traffic, single point of failure
indicators: On critical path (login, checkout, payment, data access)
Critical data (financial, health, PII, authentication credentials)
No redundancy (single point of failure, no degraded mode)
Failure blocks all users or stops revenue
examples: Authentication service (users can't log in)
Payment service (can't process orders)
API gateway (single entry point, failure blocks all traffic)
User data service (PII storage, must be available and secure)
Database cluster (all services depend on it)

overall_risk_score.description: Overall risk score determines testing thoroughness
overall_risk_score.calculation: Average of deployment_risk, integration_risk, operational_risk scores (1-3 scale)

risk_classification.description: Risk level mapped from overall risk score

integration_tests.examples: Create entity, read entity, update entity, delete entity, handle invalid input

advanced_testing.load_testing: Not required (or light load at 2x expected traffic)

examples: Logging service (writes to DB, no dependencies)
Metrics collector (standalone aggregation)
Static content API (reads from DB)
Internal utility service (simple data transformation)
low_risk.operational_testing_focus: Standard smoke tests, basic integration validation

testing_strategy.summary: Standard testing + load testing + contract testing

unit_tests.focus: Business logic, error handling, edge cases

integration_tests.scope: Comprehensive scenarios (happy path, error cases, dependency failures)
integration_tests.examples: Normal operation, dependency timeout, dependency returns error, invalid input, concurrency

contract_tests.scope: Validate API contracts with consumers and providers
contract_tests.tools: Pact, Spring Cloud Contract, or OpenAPI validation
contract_tests.purpose: Ensure API changes don't break consumers

load_tests.success_criteria: p95 latency < 500ms, no errors at 2x load

advanced_testing.chaos_testing: Not required (but recommended for services with 2+ dependencies)
advanced_testing.security_pentesting: Not required (standard OWASP scans + dependency scanning)

examples: Authentication service (JWT tokens, user validation)
Notification service (emails, SMS, push notifications)
Search API (Elasticsearch, moderate traffic)
User profile service (moderate traffic, some dependencies)
medium_risk.operational_testing_focus: Load testing, contract validation, dependency failure handling
medium_risk.prototype_recommended: Optional (if unfamiliar tech stack or complex deployment)

testing_strategy.summary: Standard + load + chaos + failover + security pentesting

unit_tests.focus: All business logic, error handling, edge cases, security paths

integration_tests.examples: Normal operation, all error cases, dependency failures, circuit breaker trips, fallback mechanisms, concurrency, race conditions

contract_tests.scope: Full contract validation with all consumers and providers
contract_tests.backward_compatibility: Strict validation - breaking changes require versioning

load_tests.success_criteria: p95 latency < 500ms at 5x load, p99 < 1000ms, no errors
load_tests.spike_testing: Test sudden traffic spikes (0 to peak in 1 minute)

chaos_tests.success_criteria: Service continues operating, degrades gracefully, recovers automatically

failover_tests.scope: Validate high availability and disaster recovery
scenarios: Database failover (primary DB fails, switch to replica)
failover_tests.success_criteria: Failover completes in < 30 seconds, no data loss, no user-visible errors

tests: OWASP Top 10 (injection, XSS, broken auth, etc.)

examples: Payment service (financial transactions, PCI compliance)
User authentication service (security-critical)
API gateway (single entry point, high traffic)
User data service (PII storage, GDPR compliance)
Database cluster (single point of failure for all services)
high_risk.operational_testing_focus: Comprehensive operational testing - chaos, load, failover, security, disaster recovery
high_risk.prototype_rationale: High-risk services MUST validate architecture assumptions early with 2-4 hour prototype (D-01-A06)

testing_requirements_summary.description: Testing requirements based on risk classification
testing_requirements_summary.medium_risk: 80% coverage, integration tests, contract tests, load tests (2x traffic)
testing_requirements_summary.high_risk: 85% coverage, comprehensive integration/contract tests, load tests (5x traffic), chaos tests, failover tests, security pentesting

development_impact.description: How risk level affects development workflow

low_risk.prove_it_works_gates: Standard validation (service starts, basic smoke test)

medium_risk.prototype: Optional, recommended if unfamiliar tech stack (D-01-A06)
medium_risk.prove_it_works_gates: Enhanced validation (smoke tests include dependency scenarios)

high_risk.prototype: REQUIRED - 2-4 hour prototype to validate assumptions (D-01-A06)
high_risk.prove_it_works_gates: Strict validation (comprehensive smoke tests, all scenarios)
high_risk.d_06_5_validation: Comprehensive validation - all checks must pass before operational testing

example_risk_assessments.description: Example assessments for common service types

example_1_low_risk.service_description: Accepts log messages via HTTP, writes to PostgreSQL, no dependencies

deployment_risk.rationale: Simple FastAPI service, familiar Python stack, single container, minimal config (5 env vars)

integration_risk.rationale: No service dependencies, writes to DB only, fully standalone

operational_risk.rationale: Not on critical path, logs can be buffered temporarily, low traffic (< 50 req/sec), failure doesn't block users

example_1_low_risk.testing_strategy: Standard testing - 80% unit coverage, integration tests, smoke tests

example_2_medium_risk.service_description: Sends emails and SMS, calls user service for contact details, publishes events

deployment_risk.rationale: Moderate complexity - uses SendGrid API + Twilio API, background Celery workers, Redis queue, 15 env vars

integration_risk.rationale: Calls user service asynchronously for contact details, external APIs (SendGrid, Twilio), circuit breakers implemented

operational_risk.rationale: Important feature but not critical path, moderate traffic (200 req/sec), can queue notifications for later, degraded mode returns 'queued' status

example_2_medium_risk.testing_strategy: Standard + contract tests (user service API) + load tests (2x traffic = 400 req/sec)

example_3_high_risk.service_description: Processes payments via Stripe, handles refunds, stores transaction history, critical for checkout

deployment_risk.rationale: Moderate deployment complexity - single container but complex Stripe integration, 25 env vars including sensitive keys, requires Stripe webhook configuration

integration_risk.rationale: Synchronous dependency on Stripe API (payment gateway), calls user service for customer details, calls order service to update order status, tight coupling - payment failure blocks checkout

operational_risk.rationale: CRITICAL PATH - payment failure stops revenue, high traffic during sales (1500 req/sec sustained), handles financial data (PCI compliance), single point of failure for checkout flow

example_3_high_risk.testing_strategy: Comprehensive - 85% coverage, contract tests, load tests (5x = 7500 req/sec), chaos (Stripe API failure, timeout scenarios), failover (Stripe outage, fallback to queued processing), security pentesting (PCI compliance validation)

operational_testing_objectives.relationship: Risk level determines operational testing objectives - high-risk services need stricter acceptance criteria

system_test_strategy.relationship: System test strategy aggregates risk assessments to determine which services need chaos/load/failover tests

service_architecture.relationship: Service architecture provides deployment complexity, dependencies, and operational characteristics used in risk assessment

d_01_a06_prototype.relationship: High-risk services (>= 2.6) MUST create rapid prototype to validate assumptions early

d_0x_a99_gates.relationship: Prove-it-works gates are stricter for high-risk services (comprehensive smoke tests vs basic validation)

d_06_5_validation.relationship: High-risk services require all D-06.5 validation checks to pass before operational testing

to_05_operational_testing.relationship: High-risk services get comprehensive operational testing (chaos, load, failover); low-risk get standard tests

llm_agent_guidance.honesty: Be honest about risk - underestimating leads to production failures. Common high-risk indicators: payment, auth, data storage, API gateway, SPOF
llm_agent_guidance.rationale_required: Document rationale for each risk score - future maintainers need to understand WHY service is high/low risk
llm_agent_guidance.no_gut_feelings: Use objective factors from severity_levels, not subjective 'feels risky' assessments
llm_agent_guidance.ask_clarifying_questions: If service description is vague, ask user about traffic volume, criticality, dependencies before scoring
llm_agent_guidance.risk_feeds_into: Risk assessment informs: (1) operational testing objectives (A09), (2) system test strategy (SE-06-A05), (3) operational testing (TO-05), (4) prototyping (D-01-A06), (5) prove-it-works gates (D-02-A99+)
llm_agent_guidance.high_risk_examples: Payment processing, user authentication, API gateway, user data storage, single points of failure, services handling PII/financial data
llm_agent_guidance.low_risk_examples: Logging, metrics, static content, internal utilities, background jobs without strict SLAs
llm_agent_guidance.when_in_doubt: If factors span multiple severity levels, choose higher severity (err on side of caution) and document why

metadata.usage: Used by SE-02-A10 during service architecture specification
